frontPage.headline: The S&P 500 is in a correction. Bear markets and recessions don't always follow
frontPage.summary: CNBC reports the November sell-off has so far pushed the S&P 500 into a correction, and notes that history shows a correction does not always lead to a bear market or a recession.
frontPage.whyItMatters: A correction is a drawdown, not a verdict; the AI-spending and funding questions behind it decide whether it deepens.

frontPage.headline: Nvidia’s stock has tumbled 28% over one chaotic month. The next big test lies in the week ahead
frontPage.summary: MarketWatch reports Nvidia's stock has tumbled 28% over one chaotic month, and that Jensen Huang faces tough questions from Congress this week.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Congressional scrutiny of the leading AI chip supplier adds policy risk on top of export-rule uncertainty for AI infrastructure plans.

frontPage.headline: Nvidia Halts Sales to Southeast Asia as U.S. Tightens China Restrictions
frontPage.summary: The New York Times reports Nvidia halted sales to four Southeast Asian countries after a new U.S. rule that would require licenses for companies there to buy advanced AI chips.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Teams planning GPU capacity that touches Southeast Asia should expect delays and stricter checks on who may buy or rent it.

frontPage.headline: Software giant SAP confirms cyber incident amid reports of source code breach
frontPage.summary: The Record reports SAP confirmed a cybersecurity incident after reports that hackers infiltrated its software development infrastructure, potentially reaching its source code. BleepingComputer reports SAP said it took urgent action to protect customers after detecting suspicious activity in its IT environment.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Source-code exposure at a major enterprise vendor is a supply-chain concern for every customer running its software in production.

frontPage.headline: US Air Force cloud platform reportedly hacked in latest federal breach
frontPage.summary: BleepingComputer reports hackers have reportedly breached the US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, adding to a recent wave of attacks on US government agencies including the FBI, CIA and Treasury Department.
frontPage.whyItMatters: A run of federal cloud breaches raises the bar for tenant isolation and credential hygiene on government-hosted platforms.

frontPage.headline: FCC approves SpaceX application to deploy one million satellites for data centers in space
frontPage.summary: Data Center Dynamics reports the FCC approved SpaceX's application to deploy one million satellites for data centers in space.
frontPage.whyItMatters: Approval grants permission, not capacity; whether orbital compute can match terrestrial power and cooling economics is unproven.

bearCase.subject: AI lab economics
bearCase.summary: MarketWatch argues that while consumption of AI tokens is exploding, which helps frontier model labs, they do not appear to be generating revenue from it at the same rate.

items.headline: Tech Stocks Rise as Investors Take a Break From AI Jitters
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports shares rebounded at the start of a shorter trading session, with all three major indexes poised to end the week strong.

items.headline: German software firm SAP is reportedly cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI push
items.summary: CNBC reports SAP is reportedly considering cutting 10,000 jobs as it reshapes its software business around AI.

items.headline: Chinese chip stocks notch biggest ever one-day gains as Beijing signals broader market support
items.summary: CNBC reports Chinese stocks rebounded sharply after a rare intraday state media readout cheered investors, as top policymakers pledged market liquidity support.

items.headline: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Key Labor Data in Focus Ahead of Fed’s December Rate Decision
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal says U.S. labor market data, including the key nonfarm payrolls report, will be in focus in the week starting Nov. 30.

items.headline: Allstate Joins Growing List of Companies Hit by Tech Outages
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports a multiday outage has left Allstate customers struggling to reach the insurer during one of the year's busiest travel weeks.

items.headline: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
items.summary: The Register reports network operators face waits of up to 18 months for equipment as telcos compete with datacenters for components. RETN says optical equipment prices are up around 50% this year.

items.headline: SpaceX installs $250m worth of Tesla Megapack batteries at Starbase data center site in Texas - report
items.summary: Data Center Dynamics reports, citing a report, that SpaceX installed $250m of Tesla Megapack batteries at its Starbase data center site in Texas. The company is seeking to develop up to $24bn of data center and natural gas power plant there.

items.headline: Galaxy Digital files for next phase of development at Helios data center campus in Texas
items.summary: Data Center Dynamics reports Galaxy Digital filed for the next phase of development at its Helios data center campus in Texas, looking to build another building at the CoreWeave-leased campus.

items.headline: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
items.summary: The Register reports datacenter spending in Europe is booming, but the models, the chips and the clout all live in the US and Asia.

items.headline: UK government rejects national consultation on AI datacenters
items.summary: The Register reports the UK government rejected a national consultation on AI datacenters, pointing to project-level environmental checks as a petition passed 39,000 signatures.

items.headline: Risky Bulletin: Hackers breach Erlang and Elixir package manager
items.summary: Risky Business reports hackers breached the Erlang and Elixir package manager. The bulletin also notes FinCEN is investigating a security breach and 1Password was hacked through an employee GitHub account.

items.headline: British government takes services offline following ‘cyber incident’
items.summary: The Record reports the UK Department for Work and Pensions said it experienced a cyber incident and took several services down as a precaution.

items.headline: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports a 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's NFS server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges.

items.headline: Drupal warns of new site takeover flaw exploited in attacks
items.summary: BleepingComputer reports the Drupal security team says attackers are exploiting a second critical vulnerability that lets them breach and hijack unpatched websites.

items.headline: Bank of England Urges Firms to Move Faster on Quantum Security
items.summary: The Quantum Insider reports the Bank of England urged the financial firms most important to UK stability to move faster than the national timetable for adopting quantum-resistant cryptography, warning that delays at a single technology provider could disrupt several firms at once.

items.headline: Guest Post: Why Critical Infrastructure Must Prepare for Cryptographic Uncertainty
items.summary: In a guest post for The Quantum Insider, Scott Aaronson argues that companies preparing for quantum computers may face a cryptographic threat that requires no quantum computer at all, and addresses operators of critical infrastructure.

items.headline: Meta Brings Code Review Auto-Approval More Mainstream with PyTorch GreenLight
items.summary: InfoQ reports PyTorch now lets an AI reviewer approve pull requests from its own maintainers. GreenLight is an open-source take on Meta's RADAR, which auto-lands low-risk diffs after safety checks, a risk score and an LLM review.
items.whyItMatters: Automated approval for low-risk changes shifts human review toward risky diffs, which makes the risk-scoring step the control to design carefully.

items.headline: Netflix Builds Quasar to Measure the Blast Radius of Library API Changes
items.summary: InfoQ reports Netflix built Quasar, an internal tool that combines semantic code indexing and API comparisons to find downstream consumers affected by library changes. It uses SCIP, Amazon S3 and Athena, and Netflix is exploring agent-assisted consumer migrations.
items.whyItMatters: Knowing the blast radius of an API change before release is a practical way to cut migration risk in a large service estate.

items.headline: QCon San Francisco 2026: How to Kill the Code Review
items.summary: InfoQ reports Ankit Jain of Aviator told QCon San Francisco 2026 that line-by-line code review is fading, since most review comments concern knowledge sharing rather than defects and over 75% of PRs merge without human review. His team reports merging four times more PRs with about 40% fewer reverts.

items.headline: Deterministic Simulation Testing
items.summary: Martin Fowler's site hosts Unmesh Joshi's description of deterministic simulation testing, which replaces real clocks, networks and storage with simulated components driven by a single-threaded execution loop. This allows simulating hard failures and routine slowdowns such as latency spikes.

items.headline: Presentation: From Fan-Out to Fast: Sub-100ms API Design in Distributed Systems
items.summary: InfoQ publishes a talk in which Saranya Vedagiri explains designing low-latency distributed APIs under 100ms, drawing on her work at eBay. Topics include hop-by-hop latency budgets, async fan-out tradeoffs, thread pool sizing, caching and circuit breakers.

items.headline: ‘Aether & Iron’: Seattle-area indie game studio builds a noir detective RPG in the sky
items.summary: GeekWire reports Issaquah, Wash., studio Seismic Squirrel is building Aether & Iron, a 30-hour noir detective RPG set in a flying 1938 New York, with turn-based combat fought from customized cars.

items.headline: Trump defends Putin friendship that Zelensky calls ‘strange’
items.summary: The Washington Post reports President Trump defended his friendship with Putin, which Zelensky calls strange, saying "We want to make a deal" and blaming the Russian and Ukrainian leaders' hate as the biggest obstacle to peace.

items.headline: Iran imposes sweeping austerity measures as U.S. economic pressure mounts
items.summary: The Washington Post reports Iran is rolling back subsidies on bread and gasoline, deepening discontent amid a worsening economic crisis after nearly nine months of war.

items.headline: France Slips Into Recession as Exports Sag
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports the French economy tipped into recession in the third quarter as summer heat waves slowed Airbus's factories.

items.headline: Bipartisan Desire to Regulate A.I. Faces Obstacles in Congress
items.summary: The New York Times reports members of both parties say they want to tackle AI policy, but the slow pace of legislating and turf battles could stand in the way.

items.headline: EU leaders fail to break $1.7 trillion budget deadlock as political pressure mounts
items.summary: CNBC reports EU leaders failed to break a deadlock over the bloc's $1.7 trillion budget, with talks set to resume in December as a key deadline looms.

items.headline: India-U.S. trade deal is close to culmination: Goyal
items.summary: The Hindu reports Commerce Minister Goyal said the process and pathway for finalising a trade pact with the U.S. is taking shape, after a USTR report proposed 25% tariffs on Indian imports, capped at 17% if a deal is agreed.

items.headline: Rupee nosedives 60 paise to settle at 92.98 against U.S. dollar
items.summary: The Hindu reports the rupee fell 60 paise to settle at 92.98 against the U.S. dollar (provisional), after touching a day's low of 93.01.

items.headline: RBI cuts daily CRR maintenance to 90%, to unlock over ₹40,000 crore
items.summary: The Hindu reports the RBI cut the daily CRR maintenance requirement to 90%, which is expected to unlock over ₹40,000 crore and improve banks' liquidity flexibility.

items.headline: MeitY plans to expand national computing capacity for AI inference
items.summary: The Hindu reports MeitY plans to expand national computing capacity for AI inference, to meet the government's own needs as well as those of research institutions, academic institutions and innovators.

items.headline: Shipping 100+ PRs to production in a week
items.summary: Will Larson of Irrational Exuberance reports shipping 100+ pull requests to production in a week, reaching 115 the week of November 9th.

items.headline: Engineering leaders can’t prove AI is paying off
items.summary: LeadDev reports what 165 engineering leaders said at LeadDev Berlin 2026, under the headline that they cannot prove AI is paying off.

items.headline: How Anthropic builds software in 2026 with Katelyn Lesse
items.summary: The Pragmatic Engineer interviews Katelyn Lesse, who explains how Anthropic rewrote Claude's API in Rust and how AI agents are changing engineering at the company.

items.headline: Fragments: November 20
items.summary: Martin Fowler's fragments relay an experiment by Marcus Borg on whether healthy code is cheaper for agents to review. Between a typical unhealthy pull request (CodeHealth 2.8) and a typical healthy one (9.7), the difference adds up to 22 to 35%; it covered three LLMs and 465 pull requests on 246 open source repositories.

items.headline: Code ownership is eroding
items.summary: LeadDev reports that less experienced developers trust AI more, under the headline that code ownership is eroding.

learn.title: Build first, reconcile later: the Explorer Pattern
learn.body:
The Explorer Pattern is a way of building something new without waiting for every team to agree first. One person or team builds a working implementation while keeping cross-team and cross-functional impact as small as possible. Only after the prototype runs do they reconcile the details with other teams. Will Larson's tl;dr says plainly that this can mean very substantial rework of the first version. Imprint previously called the same approach its "Tech-led" or "Engineering-led" development model.

The trade is deliberate. Early alignment meetings are good at surfacing constraints, but they are poor at telling anyone what the product should be. A working prototype turns a debate about hypotheticals into a conversation about something concrete, which is cheaper to argue with. The cost is that the explorer will probably build parts that other teams then ask to change.

A concrete illustration (mine, not from the source): an architect wants a new internal event pipeline. Instead of circulating a design for three weeks, one small team builds a thin end-to-end version against one real producer and one real consumer. Security, data and platform teams then review running code, and their objections arrive as specific changes.

What to take into your own work:

First, say out loud that the first version is expected to be reworked. If stakeholders treat the prototype as the plan, the pattern fails and the explorer is blamed for rework that was always priced in.

Second, keep the blast radius small on purpose. The definition hinges on minimising cross-team impact, so the prototype should not touch shared schemas, shared infrastructure or other teams' on-call load.

Third, schedule the reconciliation. The pattern has two halves, and skipping the second turns an experiment into an unreviewed production system.

Fourth, choose it selectively. It suits uncertain product invention. It suits well-understood changes to shared systems much less, where early agreement is cheaper than rework.

This note is written from the article's summary paragraph, as the full page could not be opened in this session.
